private_note: Birch (52) is still best for us, but it can't pass. Delegates 1, 3, 5, 6, 9, 10 and 12 all reject Birch and Hazel. Cedar can't pass either: five of us will block it. Alder (48) beats Today (46), guarantees health coverage, and is the only plan the Cedar side has said it could accept. Holding out for Birch probably leaves us with Today for a generation. Two thousand dollars and coverage beats nothing. I'll still block Cedar to the end.
statement: I listened to everyone and did the arithmetic. Cedar has seven votes, but five of us will vote against it to the end, so it can't reach nine. Birch and Hazel can't reach nine either, because seven of you have said no to them. That leaves one plan that people on both sides have called acceptable: Alder. Delegates 1, 5 and 10 said they'd meet us there, and 2, 7, 8 and 11 have said they could support it. So I'm moving Alder to first. Birch would do more for my family, but I'd rather leave here with a guaranteed floor and health coverage than leave with today's system for a generation. Counting me, that's eight. We need one more. Delegates 3, 6, 9 and 12: Alder costs the top groups only a few percent and otherwise runs the economy much as it does today. Will one of you join us?
